description: The same approval and draft addressed to a different recipient is a different delivery.
why_it_exists: The WF4 outbound delivery key was once derived with $now in the basis, so a second attempt at the same approved delivery produced a different send_key and a different communication_id. An uncertain send result (a timeout after the message had actually gone) therefore resolved to a brand new row on retry, and the same letter could be sent to an insurer twice with no duplicate detectable anywhere in the register. The recipient is part of the delivery identity: a letter sent to a second insurer must not be suppressed because the first insurer already received one under the same approval.

expect.note: The original oracle hashes were computed by a separate Python FNV-1a implementation over the REAL recipient address. That address has been replaced by a same-length synthetic address, so the expected hash must be regenerated from this input with an independent FNV-1a implementation before this assertion means anything. Do not copy the value the JavaScript under test produces. The original assertion was send_key === "SND-13902296".

assertions: send_key differs from the first-send key
send_key equals "SND-" + the independently computed FNV-1a of "apr=APR-001 act=ACT-001 draft=DFT-001 chan=GMAIL to=claimsotherins@example.com"
